What it is

The paper's story: where it is used, its core idea and the real system demo.
Real-world use

A phone held to the chest, a fingertip over its camera

Imagine a clinic in a low-resource area, with no ECG and PPG system: a phone times the pulse.

the authors' video · the phone on the chest

It shows The authors' own video: a seated person holds the phone to the chest and puts a fingertip over its camera; the app draws both signals.

How to read it Watch the finger cover the camera and the flash light it red; the screen then shows the pulse and the heartbeat.

drag to turn the space
Hospital · Sensing World ›
Motivation

Blood pressure changes through the day; a cuff measures it once

  1. 1patients typically only perform arm cuff-based measurements once a day
  2. 2cannot capture the fluctuations in BP
  3. 3PEP is variable up to tens of milliseconds
  4. 4PCG captures the closing of the valves sound, not the opening
an arm cuff, once a day

It shows A day of blood pressure, rising with exercise and stress, and the one point a daily cuff reading catches.

How to read it The line is the day's pressure and the dot the cuff's one reading, so all the changes between readings are missed.

ECG start, finger pulse: PEP inside

It shows The ECG's R-wave, the valve opening and the pulse at the finger: the R-wave comes a varying PEP before the valve opens.

How to read it PAT runs from the R-wave to the pulse and PTT from the valve opening, so PAT moves with PEP even when PTT stays.

heart sound: the valves closing

It shows The heart sound a microphone hears, set against the moment the aortic valve opens: the sound comes from valves closing.

How to read it The sound's burst and the valve opening are marked; the gap between them is the error of starting the clock at the sound.

State of the art

PTT on a phone alone started its clock at the wrong moment

  1. 1they use custom hardware with ultra low-noise accelerometers
  2. 2Other work has mainly focused on using the sound created by the heart
  3. 3There is currently a gap in using built-in smartphone sensors to accurately capture PTT

It shows Earlier ways to time the pulse, by where they start the clock and what hardware they need: none starts at the valve with a phone.

How to read it Up means a truer start of the beat, from the heart sound to the valve opening; right means less hardware, down to a phone.

Background

Four terms used throughout

Pulse transit time (PTT)01

the time taken by the heart's pulse to propagate between two arterial sites

Seismocardiography (SCG)02

The SCG is captured using the phone's accelerometer pressed against the chest

Photoplethysmogram (PPG)03

the camera, which then captures the photoplethysmogram (PPG) at the finger

Aortic valve opening (AO)04

the blood is ejected from the heart as the aortic valve opens

one heartbeat, at the chest and at the finger

It shows One heartbeat as the phone records it: the chest's shake (SCG, blue) and the fingertip's pulse (PPG, red).

How to read it Time runs left to right: the tall blue spike is the valve opening, and the red rise after it is the pulse reaching the finger.

Core idea

The delay from valve opening to fingertip pulse tracks pressure

  1. 1accelerometer to measure the vibration caused by the heart valve movements
  2. 2camera to measure the pulse at the fingertip
  3. 3pulse transit time (PTT) which is inversely related to BP
  4. 4an individualized calibration of PTT to BP is generated
the valve opens, the pulse arrives

It shows The chest's shake (SCG, blue) and the finger's pulse (PPG, red) over one beat, with the valve opening and the pulse's arrival marked.

How to read it The gap between the two marks is PTT, and the bracket shows it getting shorter when blood pressure rises.

Core idea · what to observe

Beat after beat, AO comes first, then the pulse

the time difference is calculated for each AO and APG peak pair

PTT-based techniques can measure beat-to-beat BP

  1. Each beat: a spike at the chest, the valve opening
  2. Later, the pulse reaches the fingertip
  3. The gap between them is one beat's PTT
  4. The median over 30 seconds is the reading
PTT, median –
Heart rate –
SCG at AO –
SCG and PPG, beat by beat

It shows The chest's SCG and the finger's PPG, with AO and the APG peak marked each beat, so their gap, the PTT, is read.

How to read it Time runs left to right: blue is the SCG in mg, red the PPG and APG, gold dots AO, red dots arrival, brackets each PTT.

Challenge 1 · unsynced sensors

The camera and the accelerometer keep different clocks

The Android SDK does not guarantee perfect synchronization between different sensor subsystems

hence we need to synchronize the data collected from the camera and the accelerometer subsystems

  1. New: two clocks, the camera's and the accelerometer's
  2. The accelerometer's samples come stamped with its own clock
  3. The clocks differ by about 170 ms, as long as a PTT
  4. So the reading is far from the true PTT
PTT read –
True PTT –
two clocks

It shows The SCG as the accelerometer stamps it sits far off the camera's clock, so its AO, and the PTT read from it, are wrong.

How to read it Red: the PPG and its arrival; blue: the SCG as stamped; gold brackets: each PTT read. Right, as in Fig. 3: blue mic audio, orange z-axis.

Solution 1 · Three beeps

Three beeps align the accelerometer with the camera

the phone’s speaker plays a series of three beeps

The timing delay is then used to shift the accelerometer signal

  1. New: the speaker plays three beeps
  2. The microphone hears them on the camera's clock
  3. The z-axis feels them on the accelerometer's clock
  4. A matched filter times each; the gap is the offset
  5. The SCG is shifted back by it
  6. Your turn Sync off and on: the PTT read moves
PTT read –
Offset found –
three beeps

It shows Each beep is heard twice, by the microphone on the camera's clock and by the z-axis on the accelerometer's, and their gap is the offset.

How to read it Time runs left to right: blue, the microphone's audio (camera clock); orange, the z-axis (accelerometer clock), as in Fig. 3; arrows mark each offset.

the SCG's timing

It shows As stamped, the SCG's AO comes late; shifted by the offset, it falls back before each arrival, and the PTT read matches.

How to read it Red: the PPG and its arrival; blue: the SCG as stamped, then shifted back; gold brackets: each PTT read; numbers below.

Challenge 2 · the pulse's arrival

The pulse's arrival is a gentle turn in a slow wave

for each heartbeat, we need to find the foot of the PPG waveform, which denotes the end of diastole

The phone's back camera operates at a standard frame rate of 30 fps

  1. New: the camera, a frame every 33 ms
  2. The arrival is the PPG's foot, where diastole ends
  3. The foot is a slow turn, not a sharp peak
  4. A peak detector needs a sharp mark there
PTT, PPG foot –
True PTT –
the PPG, frame by frame

It shows At the camera's frame rate the PPG's foot is a gentle turn, so the foot found strays from the true arrival, beat to beat.

How to read it Dots are camera frames, dashed lines the true foot, shading the slow turn, gold triangles the foot found, its stray in ms under it.

Solution 2 · APG peak

The APG peak marks the pulse's arrival

we use the second derivative of the PPG signal, called acceleration photoplethysmogram (APG)

the peak of the APG accentuates when the pulse shows up at the finger

  1. New: an FFT gives the heart rate
  2. It sets the gap between pulses
  3. The APG, the second derivative, peaks at each foot
  4. A peak detector finds each APG peak
  5. The PTT read is now right
  6. Your turn APG off and on: the PTT read moves
PTT read –
True PTT –
the APG and its peaks

It shows The PPG's second derivative, the APG, peaks sharply where the pulse arrives, so its peaks time each beat better than the foot.

How to read it PPG frames on top, the APG below with red peaks lined up to them, and on the right the spectrum, peaking at the heart rate.

Challenge 3 · finding AO

The heart's shake is faint, and its shape changes

the relative amplitude of each movement changes depending on the person and position

those recorded closer to the sternum, the MA point can have a similar prominence as the IM point

  1. New: the raw accelerometer, with breathing and heart sound
  2. The beat's shape changes with the person and the place
  3. Near the sternum, MA can dip about as deep as IM
  4. Taking MA for IM puts AO too late
PTT, boxed beat –
Error, boxed beat –
Median PTT –
SCG shapes

It shows Fig. 4's three SCG beat shapes, which change with the person and the phone's place; the model's beat now is lit.

How to read it Each beat, band-passed, runs left to right: MC up, IM down, AO up, MA down; each shape is scaled to its own height.

the AO search

It shows The SCG before each pulse arrival; with no IM check, at the sternum MA is taken for IM, so AO lands late and PTT is short.

How to read it Box: the beat the readouts read, its MC, IM, true AO and MA dotted and named; AO found: the search's pick; its error is its PTT less its true PTT. Grey: raw; blue: its slow part, breathing, four times taller; gold: band-passed; ring: picked IM; thin line: the true PTT; no AO: a beat left out.

Solution 3 · IM-guided search

An AO search guided by each APG peak

a bandpass filter from 0.8-20Hz is applied

if the ratio of their prominence is above 90%, the algorithm chooses the peak ahead of the most prominent peak as the actual IM

  1. New: the band-pass removes breathing
  2. Each APG peak opens a search window
  3. The most prominent dip is taken as IM
  4. Over 90 %, the deepest dip is MA
  5. AO: the next peak; PTT: the median gap
  6. Your turn Switch both off
Median PTT, 30 s –
True PTT, 30 s –
Error, 30 s –
SCG shapes

It shows Fig. 4's three SCG beat shapes, which change with the person and the phone's place; the model's beat now is lit.

How to read it Each beat, band-passed, runs left to right: MC up, IM down, AO up, MA down; each shape is scaled to its own height.

the AO search

It shows The paper's search acted out: filter, a window before each APG peak, IM with its check, then AO, so PTT lands on the truth.

How to read it Gold: band-passed; shaded: search window; rings: IM and MA; triangle: AO found and its PTT; thin line: true PTT; no AO: beat dropped.

Challenge 4 · PTT to blood pressure

PTT alone gives no diastolic pressure in mmHg

PTT can only estimate relative changes in blood pressureThe paper lists a third limit of PTT beside this one and the person's own curve: PTT is most strongly influenced by diastolic pressure, so the paper tests diastolic pressure (DBP) only.

the relationship between PTT and BP is dependent on the physiological properties of an individual

  1. Two people, the same PTT
  2. Their pressures differ by tens of mmHg
  3. Each person has a curve of their own
  4. One shared curve misreads both
PTT, subject A –
Cuff DBP, A –
DBP by B's curve –
Error, B's curve –
two people, two curves

It shows Day 1 of two subjects: the same PTT means a different DBP for each, so PTT needs each person's own curve.

How to read it Across: PTT (ms); up: cuff DBP (mmHg); gold: subject A, blue: subject B; dots: day 1; lines: each fit; upright dashes: A's PTT now.

A read with B's curve

It shows A's DBP over day 1's rides, by cuff and read through B's curve: the change is followed, the level is not.

How to read it Across: the rides, rest to full effort and back; up: DBP (mmHg); gold: A's cuff; blue dashes: A's PTT through B's curve.

Solution 4 · Per-person fit

A per-person calibration on day 1

an individualized calibration for each user needs to be created

we use the data from the first day for calibration between PTT and BP

  1. Participants are asked to ride a stationary bike five timesThe paper: the bike riding intensity varies from 50%, 75%, 100%, 75%, and 50% of the participants' maximum speed. Participants biked at multiple intensities to raise their blood pressure. Blood pressure and PTT are measured 7 times: once before biking, after each ride, and after two minutes of rest.
  2. A least-squares fit gives BP = K1/PTT + K2
  3. Days 2 to 4: each PTT is read off the curve
  4. Against the cuff: this person's error
  5. Your turn Try the fit, the subject, the bike speed
Bike ride speed

the day-1 fit

It shows One subject's day-1 readings and the least-squares curve BP = K1/PTT + K2 through them (Fig. 5), fitted for this person alone.

How to read it Across: PTT (ms); up: DBP (mmHg); filled dots: day 1; hollow dots: days 2 to 4 by cuff; the line: the fit.

days 2 to 4

It shows Later readings estimated from PTT and the day-1 curve, against the cuff; the paper's R ran 0.20 to 0.77 by person (Table 1).

How to read it Across: the readings of days 2, 3 and 4; up: DBP (mmHg); line: cuff; gold dots: estimated; the ring: the reading now.

Real-to-Simulation Gap

Question How close is our simulator to the paper's study?We run the paper's protocol through our model: 7 subjects, 4 days, 7 measurements a day, day 1 calibrating each person. Our numbers stand beside Table 1 and Figs. 6 to 8.

Why our R is higher The paper's arm cuff errs too, which lowers its R; ours errs only 4 mmHg (assumed).Our mean R falls as the cuff errs more: 0.88 exact, 0.72 at 4 mmHg, 0.38 at 8 mmHg; the paper's is 0.55. Between 4 and 8 mmHg ours meets the paper's, which says some of its gap to other studies is likely its cuff.

You change
the cuff's own error (assumed)
  1. 1Your turn PressThe cuff then reads the true DBP. What error is left is the phone's own: its PTT and the fit of K1 and K2.
  2. 2Your turn PressTwice our assumed error, as a cuff that lags fast changes after a ride might read.
  3. 3Your turn PressOur assumed cuff: the paper gives no error for it. We set it so our mean RMSE lands near the paper's.

Check the Paper · 2 of 3

Ablation study

Question Which step of Seismo matters most for the PTT and the DBP?Seismo's steps: the three beeps line up the two clocks, a band-pass cleans the SCG, the APG times the pulse, the IM/MA check finds AO, the median joins the beats, and each person's own fit turns PTT into DBP.

You change
Seismo's steps: one off at a time
  1. 1Your turn PressWithout the beeps the two clocks stay about 170 ms apart. That is about as long as the PTT itself (Challenge 1).
  2. 2Your turn PressWithout the APG the pulse is timed at the PPG's own foot, which the paper takes as its arrival. On 33 ms frames that slow turn is less sharp than the APG's peak (Challenge 2).
  3. 3Your turn PressNear the sternum MA can be about as deep as IM. Without the check the search can take MA for IM, and AO lands one peak late (Challenge 3).
  4. 4Your turn PressOne curve for all seven people, not one each. The PTT is the same, but each person's PTT maps to DBP differently (Challenge 4).
  5. 5Your turn PressEvery step on again: Seismo as the paper runs it.

Comparison with related work

Question What would an ECG or a heart sound read in place of the SCG?Each method starts the clock at a different event of the beat: the ECG's R-wave, the valves closing (heart sound) or the aortic valve opening (Seismo's SCG). The clock stops when the pulse reaches the finger.

You change
which event starts the clock
  1. 1Your turn PressThe R-wave comes before the valve opens by the pre-ejection period, PEP. Ours is assumed at 100 ms, changing beat to beat and with effort.
  2. 2Your turn PressS1 is the sound of the valves closing, before the opening. Phone methods [4, 8] record it with the microphone.
  3. 3Your turn PressBack to Seismo: the clock starts when the aortic valve opens.
  4. 4Your turn Drag the phone up the chestNear the clavicle the SCG's shape changes (Fig. 4), and with it the beat each method is read on.

The ECG spike and the S1 burst are drawn at the chain's times; their shapes are ours.our average correlation between PTT and DBP is comparatively high at 0.55 systems using a combination of ECG and PPG to measure PTT are actually measuring Pulse Arrival Time (PAT=PEP+PTT) to estimate BP, by wrongly assuming PEP to be constant PCG does not provide the correct time to determine PTT, as PCG captures the closing of the valves sound, not the opening

the phone on the chest

It shows Where the phone sits on the chest's left side: higher up, the SCG changes shape, as Fig. 4 shows.

How to read it The chest from the front, cm; drag the phone between the line below the pectoral and the line below the clavicle.

one beat, three starts: R-wave, AO, S1

It shows One beat as each method sees it: only the valve's opening gives the true PTT; the R-wave adds PEP, and S1 comes too early.

How to read it Rows ECG, SCG, heart sound and PPG, Fig. 2 drawing all but the heart sound; dashed lines mark each start, the method picked bold.

R with DBP: the paper's sources and ours

It shows The correlations the paper cites for ECG timing and AO timing, beside our study's R for each method: AO timing tracks DBP better.

How to read it R runs right; a dot is a mean, a bar its range or ± spread; the paper's rows first, ours coloured by method.

Go Beyond the Paper · 1 of 3

Generalization study

Question When does Seismo stop finding the heart's AO peak?The paper removed two of nine people: one with a shaking hand, one with a weak SCG through thick tissue. Here both are a number to change.

You change
the tremor, the tissue, the measurement
TremorTissueMeasurement
  1. 1Your turn Raise the tremor assumed to 10 mg.The model shakes at 6 Hz, inside the SCG's 0.8–20 Hz band, so the filter cannot take it off. Its level and its 6 Hz are ours; the paper says only that it is of similar frequency to the SCG.
AO found right –
PTT error –

What you saw AO found right: the share of beats whose AO is within 10 ms of the true AO, over three 30 s runs.as SCG is of similar frequency to his hand tremor, most AO peaks are masked

  1. 1Your turn Lower the tissue gain to 0.2.Fat and muscle between heart and phone damp the beat. Below a gain of about 0.45 the model also weakens AO against IM and MA (assumed).
  2. 2Your turn Then set the bike ride speed to 100 %.For the one participant with thick tissue, the paper says the participant's “increase in cardiac output” in the hardest rides gave a stronger SCG. The model scales the SCG by (1 + effort/100), assumed.
    Bike ride speed
AO found right –
Beat shape –

What you saw The paper says the weak signal was worst at rest; during the hardest rides the stronger SCG was found reliably (Discussion: Limitations).We suspect this is due to low acceleration caused by dampening by fat and muscle tissues

  1. 1Your turn Shorten the measurement to 10 s.The PTT is the median over the beats of one measurement. A shorter one has fewer beats to take the median of.
  2. 2Your turn Then pick another subject.Each subject has their own DBP range (Table 1) and their own K₁ and K₂ (assumed, spread about the model's reading of Fig. 5's line).
PTT error –
DBP error –

What you saw DBP error: the root mean square over three runs, each as long as the Measurement slider sets, against the model's true DBP, calibrated on day 1.Each Seismo measurement takes 30 seconds

the tab's setting swept

It shows How well Seismo finds AO as the tab's setting changes, so the point where it stops working can be seen.

How to read it The tab's setting runs along the bottom; the curve is the model, three runs a point; the gold line “now” is the setting now.

Go Beyond the Paper · 2 of 3

Physical conditions

Question Would a better camera, accelerometer or cuff improve Seismo?The paper found the accelerometer's stock setting, 250 µg/LSB at 400 Hz, good enough against 61 µg/LSB at 2000 Hz. The camera runs at 30 fps. The paper calls the 180 µg/√Hz noise floor a limit of the sensor. Here the model changes each one.

You change
the frame rate, the noise floor, the cuff's error
Frame rateAccelerometerCuff and camera noise
  1. 1Your turn Switch the frame rate to 60 fps.At 30 fps each APG peak sits on a 33 ms grid; the median over a measurement's beats averages the grid out. The 60 fps setting is assumed: the paper gives only 30 fps.
    Frame rate
Beats' PTT spread –
PTT error –

What you saw Spread: the middle half of the beats' PTTs over three 30 s runs. PTT error: the median's distance from the true PTT.The phone’s back camera operates at a standard frame rate of 30 fps

  1. 1Your turn Raise the noise floor to 400 µg/√Hz.The BMI160 is 180 µg/√Hz. Over the SCG's band that comes to about 0.8 mg: our number, not the paper's. SeismoWatch's ADXL354, a lab-grade, low-noise accelerometer, is 20 µg/√Hz.
  2. 2Your turn Then sample at 2000 Hz.A faster rate spreads the same noise floor over a wider band; the filter keeps only 0.8–20 Hz, so little changes.
    Accelerometer rate
AO found right –
PTT error –

What you saw AO found right: the share of beats within 10 ms of the true AO, over three 30 s runs, the phone where it is now.the noise floor of the sensor is relatively high compared to that of a low noise accelerometer

  1. 1Your turn Raise the cuff's error to 8 mmHg.The cuff is both the calibration and the test. Its error enters the fit on day 1 and every comparison after it.
  2. 2Your turn Then raise the camera noise to 20 %.Camera noise, as a share of the pulse's height, moves each APG peak by a frame or more.
DBP RMSE –
PTT error –

What you saw DBP RMSE: this subject's protocol, day 1 calibrating, days 2–4 tested. The cuff's error and the camera's noise are the model's; the paper gives neither.it is not designed for measuring rapidly changing blood pressure

the tab's setting, at each value

It shows The tab's quantity at the paper's setting and at the others, so the gain of a better part can be read.

How to read it A bar a setting the model ran, gold the one now, grey the others; the quantity and its unit stand over the plot.

Go Beyond the Paper · 3 of 3

Device design

Question Where, and how quiet, must the accelerometer be?Seismo reads the heart with the phone's own accelerometer. The paper tries two places and sets the BMI160's noise beside the ADXL354 (a lab-grade, low-noise accelerometer) that SeismoWatch uses, to explain a lost participant.

Why it matters Under the noise, AO is lost; the ADXL354, a lab-grade, low-noise accelerometer, hears it more clearly.The colour is our assumed map: the AO's size at each place against the noise in the 0.8–20 Hz band. The paper measures only its two places.

Fixed
the person at rest
You change
place, noise, rate
You watch
